Apex Industrial Equipment Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Equipment Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press * then 1 on your telephone keypad. If your question has been answered or you would like to remove yourself from the queue, please press the # key. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Equipment Corp.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; David Reynolds, Chief Operating Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Equipment Corp.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering net market share expansion while navigating supply chain dynamics, and positioning ourselves strongly amid evolving end-market outlooks. Our strategic focus on precision growth in automation, machining, and material handling has driven robust bookings and backlog growth, even as macroeconomic pressures test demand. We've optimized our operations for resilience, invested in innovative technologies, and maintained discipline on sustainability initiatives that resonate with customers.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Kline (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. As we review our Q3 results, I'll cover our market share dynamics, supply chain updates, end-market outlook, top-line performance, book-to-bill trends, macroeconomic impacts, and forward guidance. These elements highlight our leadership in the $650 billion global industrial equipment sector, spanning automation systems, precision machining, and material handling equipment.

Starting with market share performance, a critical leading indicator for our long-term growth: Overall, we delivered a net expansion of 120 basis points year-over-year, reaching an estimated 7.2% global share in our core segments. This is our strongest quarterly gain since Q1 2022, propelled by structural tailwinds in electrification and reshoring, despite headwinds in oversupplied legacy markets. Internal tracking, corroborated by Gardner Intelligence and Roland Berger's latest Industrial Machinery Outlook, shows clear wins.

In automation and robotics—42% of our revenue—we captured 3.1 percentage points of share growth, lifting us to 14.5% globally from 11.4% a year ago. Our ApexFlex AI-enabled collaborative robot line drove 28% YoY unit growth and 12% ASP uplift through embedded edge computing and predictive maintenance. North America gained 4.2 points to 22% share, outpacing Fanuc and ABB as U.S. manufacturers like Ford and GM ramped CAPEX under the CHIPS Act and Inflation Reduction Act. Our order backlog here grew 35% quarter-over-quarter to $1.2 billion, with 92% utilization at our Rockford, Illinois facility. EMEA added 1.8 points to 13% share via EU Green Deal mandates, displacing Kuka in the German Mittelstand where our modular systems cut integration TCO by 22%. APAC held flat at 9%, pressured by Chinese OEMs like Estun and Efort, but our new JV with Yaskawa in India targets semiconductor fab automation, including pilots for Tata Electronics' Gujarat facility.

For precision machining and CNC tools—35% of revenue—we saw a modest 80 basis points share loss globally to 9.8% from 10.6%, due to cyclical softness in legacy automotive stamping, offset by premium wins. North America gained 1.5 points to 12% as aerospace primes like Boeing and Spirit AeroSystems selected our ApexPrecision 5-axis CNCs for titanium and composites, offering 15% faster cycle times and 20% lower energy via HyperCool spindle tech and IoT digital twins. APAC lost 2.1 points to 8.5%, hit by overcapacity in China, but our ApexEdge hybrid additive-subtractive platforms grabbed 15% share in eVTOL and battery gigafactories with orders from CATL and BYD; India's share held at 11% via 'Make in India' partnerships like Bharat Forge. EMEA was flat at 10%, with renewables gains from wind turbine blade routers outpacing oil & gas losses.

Material handling—23% of revenue—grew share by 1.2 points to 6.8% globally, led by electrification. Our ApexLift electric counterbalance forklifts with 48V lithium-iron-phosphate batteries and VNA capabilities gained 2.8 points in North America to 11%, displacing Toyota Industries and Hyster-Yale with 30% lower OpEx in e-commerce DCs like Amazon and Prologis; utilization exceeds 95% at Henderson, Kentucky. Latin America surprised with a 3-point gain to 9% in Brazil and Mexico via nearshoring. EMEA lost 1 point to 5% on battery regs, but Q4 EU certification sets up rebound; APAC slipped 0.5 points to 4.5%, countered by a $50 million Thailand assembly line.

Underpinning this is our Precision Growth strategy: reallocating 15% of R&D CAPEX—$180 million in FY24—to AI/ML overlays and sustainable tech, boosting win rates 18% in ESG RFPs. Our $220 million RoboTech Dynamics acquisition bolstered robotics IP, and 60% North American sourcing mitigates tariffs. We project 200-250 basis points total gain in FY25 to 8% globally, via ApexOS platform, battery manufacturing share, and pricing discipline to hold 42% gross margins, while addressing Chinese dumping and Eurozone risks.

Turning to total revenue and year-over-year growth: Q3 revenue came in at $2.847 billion, up 18.4% from $2.404 billion in Q3 2023. This is our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, with organic expansion of 14.2% excluding the $120 million from our EuroPress Hydraulics acquisition. Trailing 12-month revenue hit $11.3 billion, up 16.8%. Bookings drove a record $4.2 billion backlog, up 22% YoY, weighted 45% to high-margin automation.

By segment: Automation & Robotics at $1.213 billion, +25.7% YoY, from TitanBot cobots and AGVs in semis and EVs, with 1.45x book-to-bill and wins at Intel Ohio and Micron New York. Precision Machining & CNC at $996 million, +12.1%, strong in renewables and heavy machinery despite aero softness; VF-5000 series up 18% in wind components. Material Handling & Hydraulics at $638 million, +15.9% including EuroPress synergies of $15 million.

Regionally: North America $1.482 billion, +20.1%, on CHIPS/IIJA capex; EMEA $797 million, +14.8%, with 30% aftermarket; APAC $484 million, +22.3%, led by India and China EVs; Rest of World $84 million, +10%.

Drivers include smart factory features in 60% of orders, ESG contracts worth $300 million, and normalized lead times.

Gross margin was 42%, driven by pricing, mix, and efficiencies. Operating expenses were $450 million, yielding operating income of $650 million. Net income was $480 million, or $2.15 per share.

Our book-to-bill ratio of 1.18x—up from 1.10x in Q2 and 0.92x last year—reflects bookings of $1.42 billion against $1.20 billion billings, pushing backlog to $3.1 billion, up 22% YoY and 8% QoQ. Core ratio is 1.25x excluding legacy. Precision machining hit 1.32x on reshoring; factory automation/robotics 1.45x on cobots with Rockwell PLCs; material handling 1.15x. North America 1.35x on IIJA hydraulics; APAC 0.98x offset by India PLI; EMEA 1.10x on defense tooling. Our Smart Factory 4.0 initiative, with $250 million R&D, boosts win rates 18% via EvoLine systems and hydrogen presses. Q4 expected above 1.20x with semi/renewables pipeline.

On supply chain constraints: We've cut average BOM lead times 35% to 25 weeks via $450 million safety stock (14 weeks coverage), stabilizing turns at 8.2x. Semiconductors eased to 92% on-time for PLCs/servos, though 15-20% premiums persist from EV/AI spillovers. Metals moderated—U.S. HRC at $650/ton—but Red Sea added 2-3 weeks for HSLA steels; Europe shifted 15% sourcing to U.S./Mexico. Rare earths NdPr spiked 18% to $85/kg on China quotas, mitigated by Lynas/Australia (40%), MP Materials (30%); shortages under 3%. APAC lead times under 12 weeks; NA reshoring cut China electronics to 24%. $120 million digitization via SAP Ariba/AI flags 95% disruptions early; VMI covers 35% SKUs, offtakes lock semis 5-7% below spot. Resilient Factory 2.0 in Spartanburg fabricates 20% cabinets; additive cuts prototyping 60%; blockchain for rare earths. Q4 backlog conversion to 85%, supporting FY24 guide; $600 million cash buffers risks like Houthi freight or Taiwan issues.

Macroeconomic factors have pressured demand: Global PMI at 48.5 signals contraction, with Q3 orders down 12% YoY to reflect high rates (Fed at 5.25-5.50% deferring 20-30% capex), inflation (steel +15%, copper $4.80/lb), and geopolitics (Ukraine energy volatility down 25% oil/gas orders). Book-to-bill at 0.95x, backlog $4.8 billion up 5% sequentially. NA resilient (+2% capex, renewables +15%) but auto destocking -22%; Europe -20% on ECB/energy; APAC mixed (China robots -30%, SE Asia +8%); aerospace +10%, semis +5%, renewables +18%. Countering with AI predictive maintenance ($150 million aftermarket, 28% revenue), digital twins (40% faster leads), 40% R&D to electrification; 70% NA localization, $500 million buyback, 22.5% gross margins.

End-market outlook: Near-term (12-18 months), 4-6% global growth on PMI recovery to 52, inventory normalization. Semis (25% revenue) 8-10% on AI fabs/CHIPS $52 billion; auto 5-7% EV stabilization; aero/defense 6-8% ramps; other flat-3%. NA 5-7%, Europe 1-3%, APAC bifurcated. Medium-term (2-5 years), 7-9% CAGR: semis 12-15%, auto/EV 15-20%, aero 9-11%, renewables 10%+. NA 8% CAGR ($1T infra), Europe 5-7%, Asia 9-11%. Pillars: $450 million R&D for AI spindles/hybrids; $300 million capex ROI>25%; M&A optics. FY24 growth 8-10%, EPS 12-15%.

Guidance: Q4 revenue $2.95-3.05 billion, 17-20% YoY; FY24 $11.9-12.1 billion, +15-17%. Gross margins 28.5% +150 bps.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow. Now, I will hand over to David Reynolds, COO, for an operational update.

David Reynolds (COO):
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we've optimized our supply chain through diversification and digitization, improved manufacturing efficiency with 92% utilization across facilities like Rockford and Henderson, and enhanced customer service via IoT platforms like ApexPredict covering 45,000 assets. We're leveraging data analytics for predictive maintenance and 25% TCO reductions, while investing in employee training to build skills in AI/ML and sustainable practices. Our nearshoring in Monterrey and Spartanburg supports 85% backlog conversion.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Raj Patel, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Raj Patel (CTO):
Thank you, David. We are committed to driving innovation with cutting-edge solutions. Our R&D investments—$450 million over three years—target AI, machine learning, and IoT for predictive maintenance and operational optimization. ApexFlex cobots and ApexEdge hybrids exceed expectations, reducing cycle times 25% and capturing share in EV gigafactories and semis. Our new ApexOS platform, tailored for SMEs like Siemens MindSphere, drives 20-30% productivity gains, with 60% of shipments IoT-enabled. HyperMill for aerospace and EvoLine for batteries position us in megatrends.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press * then 1. Our first question comes from Ben Harris with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Harris (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Raj Patel (CTO):
Thanks, Ben. Automation spending is accelerating, particularly in North America and Southeast Asia, with 8-10% near-term growth in semis fabs driven by AI and CHIPS Act ramps at TSMC and Intel. Our ApexFlex line saw 28% unit growth and 1.45x book-to-bill, as OEMs like Ford prioritize reshoring and flexible cells with edge AI for 25% uptime improvements. Medium-term, expect 12-15% CAGR as Industry 4.0 hits $500 billion, where our cobots and AGVs capture share through predictive features outpacing Fanuc.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (Goldman Sachs):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Sarah Kline (CFO):
Great question, Lisa. We've reduced lead times 35% and locked multi-year offtakes for 80% of semis at 5-7% below spot, while safety stock covers 14 weeks. Pricing actions cover 80% of inflation like NdPr +18% or steel surges, with passthroughs and mix shifts expanding margins 150 bps to 42%. Digitization flags disruptions early, vertical integration fabricates 20% cabinets in-house, and 60% NA sourcing mitigates geopolitics—keeping gross margins resilient at 28.5% outlook despite Red Sea or rare earth risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly (Barclays):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Absolutely, Tom. Sustainability is core to Precision Growth: HyperCool spindles cut energy 20%, electric ApexLift forklifts slash OpEx 30%, and dry-cutting tech reduces coolant 40%. ESG wins drove 18% RFP uplift and 13% aftermarket growth. We're on track for EU Battery Reg compliance, hydrogen-ready presses, and 20% NA gigafactory share, aligning with IRA/Green Deal while targeting FY25 share gains and 25% EBITDA via data monetization.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Equipment Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Emily Carter (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
